about: The one description of Deedglass (VIRAL-3 PRD-04). docs/description_test.go checks README.md, AGENTS.md, server.json, context7.json, npm/deedglass/package.json (description and keywords), the Claude Code plugin and marketplace, the Docker catalog entry, internal/installlinks.Description (the Claude Desktop bundle and the Goose link), the docs home page's description and the docs site's llms.txt (docs-site/astro.config.mjs reads this file) against it. `short` is the tagline cut to fit Cursor's 80-character tagline (integrations/cursor/listing.json). The slogan 'See what your agents actually did.' (the CLI banner, email footers, the docs home heading) is a slogan, not a description, and stays as it is; the docs home <title> is 'Deedglass Docs' because the tagline is longer than a 60-character title. Change the wording here first, then in each file. Plain names per docs/NAMING.md. Claims: P-097 (tagline, summary; it rests on P-057, P-060, P-069), P-086 (licence), P-104 (network; it rests on P-087 and P-052).
tagline: Rules decide each AI agent tool call; Deedglass checks what really changed and seals a record.
short: Rules decide each AI agent tool call; Deedglass checks what really changed.
summary: Deedglass sits between AI agents and the systems they change. Rules decide each tool call, a check compares what the system really changed with what the agent reported (Claimed, Checked or Proven; Matches, Doesn't match or Can't check), and each result is sealed as a signed record anyone can check offline. It can undo the rows an action changed.
licence: The core, the SDKs and the CLI are Apache-2.0. The Pro features in `ee/` are FSL-1.1-ALv2, and each release of them becomes Apache-2.0 two years after it ships. The release binary, the `@deedglass/cli-*` npm packages and the container image include `ee/`, so their licence is `Apache-2.0 AND FSL-1.1-ALv2`.
network: Free features send nothing to deedglass.com. Only a machine with a Pro licence checks it, through Dodo Payments and deedglass.com: `deedglass serve` when it starts and then daily, and Pro commands when you run them; a request goes out only when the last successful check is a day old. `deedglass version --check` and the `--latest` option of `deedglass policy install` and `policy packs` contact GitHub only when you use them.
